samples.summary: `keeps a concurrent edit to another slide` never simulates a concurrent edit; its assertion is trivially true
samples.evidence: Lines 91-100: `const untouched = slides()[0]; const peerEdit = { ...untouched.elements[0] }; await controller.add(...); expect(slides()[0]).toBe(untouched); expect(slides()[0].elements[0]).toEqual(peerEdit);`. `peerEdit` is a shallow copy of the very object being compared, so line 99 follows mechanically from the identity assertion on line 98 and asserts nothing extra. No peer write happens between the read (`op(readSlidesRoot(...))`) and the `doc.update` splice, which is the window the docblock says these verbs exist to protect. Crucially, the failure mode named in the comment — `root.slides = <array>` last-write-wins — would still pass this test, because a reassigned array carrying the same slide objects preserves both identity and element equality. Real granularity coverage does exist in `slide-ops.spec.ts` (`carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck`, and the `moveAfterByIndex` in-place reorder test), which is why the impact is contained rather than major.

samples.summary: `withSref` returning `ref: null` for an orphaned sheet anchor is documented as the client's orphan signal but has no test
samples.evidence: `withSref` calls `cellAnchorToSref`, which returns `null` when the anchored rowId/colId is no longer in `rowOrder`/`colOrder` (packages/sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:22-31). The controller docblock states this is "exactly how the editor tells an orphaned thread from a live one". Grepping comments.controller.spec.ts for `ref: null` / `cellAnchorToSref` / `Tab not found` returns no matches; the only `ref` assertions are the live-cell cases (`expect(threads.map((t) => t.anchor.ref)).toEqual(['A1', 'B2'])`). Nothing fails if a future change makes an orphaned anchor report a stale or wrong A1 ref.

samples.summary: No HTTP-level test covers any of the new /api/v1 routes (comments, slides, worksheet images, board), and the CLI suite mocks HttpClient entirely
samples.evidence: Backend specs construct controllers directly (`new ApiV1CommentsController(...)`, `new ApiV1SlidesController(...)`, `new ApiV1WorksheetImagesController(...)`) and call methods, so `@Controller`/`@Get`/`@Post` paths, param names and guards are never resolved. Grepping packages/backend/test for `/comments`, `/slides`, `/reorder`, `/layouts` returns only unrelated hits (jest-e2e.json moduleNameMapper, a pptx fixture) — no e2e spec touches these routes. On the CLI side, packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts `vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js')` replaces the whole client, so the URLs in http-client.ts (`.../tabs/:id/reorder`, `.../comments/:t/comments/:c`, `.../slides/:id/duplicate`, `.../layouts`) are asserted only in the two dry-run cases (tab duplicate, board set-content); http-client-paths.test.ts covers only a hand-picked sample of older methods. A path/verb mismatch between the CLI client and the backend decorator would ship green. `route-collision.spec.ts` checks only for duplicate route strings, not that any route resolves.

samples.summary: `createThread` on a sheet with an unknown tabId (404) is untested
samples.evidence: `comments.controller.ts` throws `new NotFoundException('Tab not found')` when `doc.getRoot().sheets?.[tabId]` is absent. comments.controller.spec.ts has no test passing an unknown `tabId` — grep for `Tab not found` in that spec returns nothing; the sheet failure cases covered are only 'no stable row/column id' and 'empty body'. A regression turning this into a 500 or into a silently created thread on a missing tab would not be caught.
searchedFor: read the sheet describe block of comments.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: "Editing does not notify" is stated as deliberate behaviour but no test asserts `createFromComment` is not called on an edit
samples.evidence: `editComment` carries the comment "Editing does not notify: the recipients were told when the comment was written". The notifications describe block in comments.controller.spec.ts asserts non-notification only for reopen (`setResolved {resolved:false}`) and for self-mention. There is no `expect(notificationService.createFromComment).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` around an `editComment` call, so adding a notify to the edit path (duplicate inbox rows for the same comment) would pass every suite.
searchedFor: read the 'ApiV1CommentsController notifications' and 'edit / delete authorship' describe blocks in comments.controller.spec.ts

samples.evidence: `parsePdfAnchor` has three distinct rejections: non-integer/negative `pageIndex`, `rect` not an object, and each of x/y/w/h out of 0..1. The PDF describe block in comments.controller.spec.ts covers only the last two ('refuses a rectangle outside the page', 'refuses a negative page index'). A body with `pageIndex` and no `rect` at all — the most likely malformed agent payload — never reaches a test, so the `'rect' must be an object` guard could be deleted without any failure.
searchedFor: read 'ApiV1CommentsController on a PDF' describe block in comments.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: `add` with an unknown or non-string layoutId is untested at the controller
samples.evidence: `add` does `input.layoutId === undefined ? 'blank' : requireString(input, 'layoutId')` and hands the value straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide(layoutId, at)`. slides.controller.spec.ts only calls `add(WS, DOC, {})` and `add(WS, DOC, { index })` — no test passes `layoutId: 'does-not-exist'` or a non-string, so neither the 400 from `requireString` nor whatever the store does with an unresolvable layout (500 vs. fallback) is pinned down.

samples.summary: `stores the collection keyed by each image id` partly re-asserts its own input
samples.evidence: `expect(res).toEqual({ images: [image(), image({ id: 'img-2', anchor: 'D4' })] })` echoes the request body, since `setImages` returns `{ images }` built from the parsed input; that half of the test holds regardless of what was written to the CRDT. The subsequent assertions on `root.sheets[TAB].images` keys and `img-2.anchor` are the ones doing the work, so this is cosmetic redundancy rather than fake coverage.

`it('registers at least the controllers this spec knows about')` asserts a bare count. It does usefully guard against `Reflect.getMetadata('controllers', ApiV1Module)` silently returning `[]` (which would make the collision test vacuous), but the literal 18 will drift and carries no meaning once it does.

samples.summary: CLI `sheets images set` stdin path and a couple of dry-run previews are untested
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts drives `images set` only through `--data`; the `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` branch (and its 'Invalid JSON ... on stdin' message) has no test. Likewise `board content --dry-run` and `comments list --dry-run` previews are not asserted, though the analogous dry-run branches for tab duplicate and board set-content are.
